title: Bharata comes home
hookLine: riders who won't say why bring a prince home, and his first wish is for his older brother
carry: an elder brother stands as a father
tomorrow: what does Bharata say to his mother?
last: HONOR MOTHER AND FATHER AS GODS.

cards: Far away, in his grandfather's city, Bharata wakes up badly shaken. His friends try music and jokes, and he can't smile. He tells them his dream.
His father, pale, hair loose, smeared with oil, riding a chariot pulled by donkeys, heading south. In the epics, the south is the direction of Yama, the lord of death.
Bharata says: either I, or Rama, or Lakshmana, or the king is going to die. Then the riders from Ayodhya arrive.

teach.h: ALL IS WELL, THE RIDERS SAY.
teach.b: The messengers do exactly as they were told. There's urgent business, they say. Come at once.
Bharata asks after everyone, one by one: his father, Rama, Lakshmana, the queens. The answers are polite and not quite answers. All is well with those you ask about.
So he sets out, days on the road. Then Ayodhya appears, and something is wrong. No music.
No crowds. People avoid his eyes. He goes to his father's rooms, and his father isn't there.
So he goes to his mother.
Kaikeyi is glad to see him, and tells him, almost lightly: your father has gone the way all living things go. Bharata falls to the floor.

teach.h: WHERE IS RAMA? HE'S MY FATHER NOW.
teach.b: When he can speak, he asks: where is Rama? I want to touch his feet. He's my father now.
That line carries a Hindu teaching about dharma in the family.

Later in the Ramayana, Rama himself says that three people are to be honored as fathers: the father, the elder brother, and the one who teaches you. In a traditional Hindu family the eldest brother isn't only a sibling.

teach.h: AN ELDER BROTHER STANDS AS A FATHER.
teach.b: When the father is gone, he stands in his place, and the younger ones turn to him with a son's respect.

You can still hear it at home: a grown man calling his older brother bhaiya and asking him first before a big decision. Bharata's first thought isn't the crown. It's the brother who is now his father.
Then Kaikeyi, sure she's giving good news, tells him the rest: the two boons, the exile, the throne kept for him. She thinks she's made her son a king. He only wanted his brother.

how: Ramayana reciters tell Bharata's homecoming as its own episode: the dream, the silent city, and his first question, for Rama rather than the throne.

o: his pilgrimage to the Ganga to bathe after his wedding
his march to Lanka at the head of Rama's army
his trip home, called back without being told why

games.q: the road home — tap the pairs.
p: his father in a donkey chariot, going south

s: the messengers tell Bharata the king has died
they give careful answers and only say there's urgent business.
Bharata's first question after the news is about Rama
he asks where Rama is, so he can touch his feet.
in the dream his father is heading south
in the epics, the south is the direction of Yama, lord of death.

games.q: you're Bharata. your mother has just told you your father is dead. what do you ask first?
games.why: he asks for Rama, so he can touch his feet: with his father gone, the elder brother stands as his father.

practice: Bring to mind someone older who has looked out for you like a parent: an older brother or sister, a cousin, a teacher. Picture their face. If you pray, ask a blessing for them, the way Hindu families hold their elders in prayer.
If you don't, just say a silent thank you, and let one slow breath carry it.

wordCard.voice: Bharata's journey. Called home without being told why, Bharata learns his father is dead, and his first wish is for Rama, the brother who is now his father.

orig.note: Sanskrit svapna: a dream. in the epics, dreams often carry warnings of what's coming.

carryVoice: Your line: an elder brother stands as a father. Bharata asked for Rama before the throne. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 70–72 (the messengers; the journey; Kaikeyi tells Bharata)
Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 18 (Rama: the father, the elder brother and the teacher are to be honored as fathers)
